_comment: Created by tools/build.py of SemTS in the VOWL JSON format of OWL2VOWL 0.3.5 (http://vowl.visualdataweb.org)

description.en: SemTS is an ontology to semantically structure insights gained from multivariate time series analyses combined with domain-specific information. The concept of SemTS constitutes a specification of informative data points or intervals within time series data, further referred to as segments. Any segment comprises characteristic knowledge associated with the covered time interval. Examples of such knowledge range from common time series features and structural particularities, such as anomalies or motifs, to a priori information provided by domain experts. A classification and semantic representation of this knowledge enables organized reusability and effective propagation.

comment.en: A datatype in QUDT used to specify the data type of values (e.g., quantity values). Instances are defined in the QUDT datatype vocabulary, http://qudt.org/vocab/datatype/.
A unit of measure (e.g., meter, second). Instances are defined in the QUDT unit vocabulary, http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/.
A meaningful collection of concepts in SKOS.
An idea or notion used to support knowledge organization, the fundamental unit of SKOS.
An algorithm (method or procedure) described in the Machine Learning Schema.
A metric used to evaluate the performance or quality of an ML process or result.
A configuration parameter not learned from data that influences the behavior of an algorithm.
A specific implementation of an algorithm or method described in the Machine Learning Schema.
A learned or specified model representing the result of training or configuration.

Refers to any algorithmic solution in the context of time series analysis. While this class extends the mls:Algorithm class, it enables a reference to further details on specific task specifics and experiments. It is considered method knowledge as this class can be used to define knowledge about an appropriate or optimal algorithmic solution associated with a time series segment.

A time series segment that does not, or only partially refer to concrete time series data. It represents an artificially generated time series segment that might for instance describe the result of a forecast with a time index not being in the range of the original time series data.

Knowledge that represents contextual information whose proposition is not intrinsically scoped to a particular TimeSeriesSegment or a particular set of segments. It may nevertheless be associated with selected segments through commonContextKnowledge. The class is not disjoint with DataKnowledge, ScenarioKnowledge, or MethodKnowledge. Whenever this type is present, segment association must still use commonContextKnowledge rather than segmentKnowledge or multiSegmentKnowledge.
Defines a data dimension (or also referred to as feature or attribute) in a time series segment.
Defines knowledge derived from data. This includes statistics, signal characteristics, and knowledge generated through data-analysis methods, such as predictions, anomalies, or cluster memberships.
A KnowledgeRelation with one or more source Knowledge instances and one or more target Knowledge instances. Its semantic meaning is supplied through knowledgeConcept.

Refers to a value that is directly stored in the knowledge graph. Compared to referenced values, these values are rather single, non-complex values having a primitive type.
One example could be the mean value of a univariate time series.

A hyperparameter is considered method knowledge as this class can be used to define knowledge about an appropriate or optimal hyperparameter setting associated with the analysis of a time series segment for a concrete task.
Represents the highest level of any knowledge associated with time series data. Knowledge can be made more specific via subclasses or associated concepts.
Any knowledge that is generated by a comparison of compatible inputs. This might either be raw data or already defined knowledge. A simple example might be the result of a Euclidean distance.
An SKOS concept associated with the knowledge class or any corresponding subclass
An SKOS concept associated with the knowledge generation entity class or any corresponding subclass

Represents the highest entity to define the process of knowledge generation. A more specific description can be provided by subclasses or assigned concepts. This class inherits from prov:Activity and thus allows for provenance during knowledge propagation.

Defines any input and output of a knowledge generation entity. It inherits from prov:Entity to define instances that are used by or generated by a prov:Activity, which in turn is the parental class of a knowledge generation entity.
Defines the input of a knowledge generation entity. While outputs can only contain produced knowledge, inputs might either reference knowledge or raw data.

Defines a knowledge generation entity, which corresponds to method-based solution. Compared to other knowledge generation entities this class is a subclass of mls:Implementation and thus can be linked to algorithmic details.

Defines the output of a knowledge generation entity. Compared to inputs, outputs only allow for a reference to generated knowledge and not to raw data. This, on purpose, excludes data transformations from the overall ontology concept by only focusing on a propagation of knowledge.
A grouping of knowledge which itself is again considered knowledge. Can be used to structure knowledge and create hierarchies.

Defines the goodness or confidence of time series knowledge associated with one or multiple segments. For knowledge produced by a knowledge generation method the quality measure is often equal to the evaluation metric of the generation method, which is why this class inherits from mls:EvaluationMeasure.

To complement any knowledge that is generated via analytical methods, this class represents knowledge generated from reasoning processes. This also includes validation processes from human experts or results from reasoning tools.
While many analysis results can be regarded unvalidated predictions, this class defines subsequent evaluations to further derive concrete facts or confirmations.

Abstract Knowledge superclass for a semantic relationship among Knowledge instances. It is not intended for direct instantiation: every relation individual is directed or undirected. Relation meanings are expressed by a KnowledgeConcept from any suitable vocabulary. The core ontology imposes no fixed relation concept scheme.
Any knowledge that defines an appropriate setting, regarding a particular method that is beneficial or even optimal when analyzing a segment given a particular task.
This class describes a trained model in the traditional machine learning sense. It inherits from mls:Model and serves as a knowledge entity for subsequent predictions.
An SKOS concept associated with the quality measure class

Refers to a value that is of arbitrary complexity and not directly stored in the knowledge graph. This class inherits from dcat:Resource and can be retrieved by the associated metadata. Dataset-valued resources may additionally be typed as dcat:Dataset. Examples include documents, models, images, fragments, or generated shapelet collections.

Defines any knowledge that is associated with a particular scenario or domain. Scenario knowledge corresponds to validated expert knowledge or scenario-specific facts. It includes simple notes, predefined labels or mathematical expressions describing the underlying time series data.

Defines analytical, data-specific insights including derived statistics or other structural characteristics such as representative kernel expressions. Knowledge of this class mostly equals extracted data features.
Defines knowledge derived from data-driven analyses. This for instance includes anomalies and predictions.
Defines knowledge that relates multiple segments, for example through cross-correlation or a distance measure.

Represents a segment, also referred to as a slice, of a univariate or multivariate time series. A segment may cover the complete time series, a subinterval restricted to selected dimensions, or a single data point. The class inherits from dcat:Dataset and identifies its temporal index, represented data dimensions, distributions, and associated knowledge.
A KnowledgeRelation with at least two unordered Knowledge participants. It does not use the directed source or target roles. Its semantic meaning is supplied through knowledgeConcept.
This abstract class serves as parental class of EmbeddedValue and ReferencedValue.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'after' (OWL-Time time:intervalAfter). Inverse of :before. For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, this can be inferred from their :segmentIndex: A starts after B ends.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'before' (OWL-Time time:intervalBefore). For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, this can be inferred from their :segmentIndex temporal entities: A ends before B starts.

Associates a TimeSeriesSegment with CommonContextKnowledge that is contextually relevant under the segment conditions without asserting that the knowledge proposition is directly scoped to the segment.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'contains' (OWL-Time time:intervalContains). Inverse of :during. For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A fully contains B.
Specifies the column index of a time series segment within a data file or database, in case a source contains multiple time series (e.g. nested dataframes).
Specifies the row index of a time series segment within a data file or database, in case a source contains multiple time series (e.g. nested dataframes).
Can be used to optionally add a description to an entity of the domain.
Specifies the position of the associated dimension within a dataframe or similar ordered data structures.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'during' (OWL-Time time:intervalDuring). For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A occurs strictly within B (start and end inside B).
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'equals' (OWL-Time time:intervalEquals). For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A and B have identical start and end.

Allen’s interval algebra relation 'finishedBy' (OWL-Time time:intervalFinishedBy). Inverse of :finishes. For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A is finished by B, both end together and B starts before A.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'finishes' (OWL-Time time:intervalFinishes). For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A and B share the same end, and A starts after B.
Relates a KnowledgeGenerationEntity to an output it generated. Specialisation of prov:generated.
References any knowledge within a particular knowledge group.
Assigns a qudt:Datatype instance (for example from http://qudt.org/vocab/datatype/) to a DataDimension or to an instance of a Value subclass.
Assigns a qudt:Unit instance (for example from http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/) to a DataDimension or to an instance of a Value subclass.
Relationship to the Value class and thus to allow for a reference to stored data.
Defines the relation from a Knowledge Generation Input to a Time Series Segment and thus to metadata which specifies the underlying data.
Similar to the Input Data Reference, this relation defines all the knowledge associated with the input of a Knowledge Generation Entity.

Defines a hierarchic relationship between time series segments. The intuition of this property is to differentiate between complete time series, in a sense that it includes the data from start to end and subsegments which are reduced in time or dimensionality and thus can be considered a slice of this original data.
Relates a concept for a Knowledge instance. Can be used to assign concrete instances from the SemTS taxonomy.
Relates a concept for a Knowledge Generation instance.
Relates the Knowledge Generation Entity, which produced this Knowledge instance.
Allows to assign a quality measure to instantiated knowledge.
Relates a KnowledgeRelation to a participating Knowledge instance. It is used directly for undirected relations and is the superproperty of the directed source and target roles.
Relates a DirectedKnowledgeRelation to a Knowledge instance in the source-side role defined by the relation concept.
Relates a DirectedKnowledgeRelation to a Knowledge instance in the target-side role defined by the relation concept.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'meets' (OWL-Time time:intervalMeets). For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A ends exactly when B starts, with no overlap.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'metBy' (OWL-Time time:intervalMetBy). Inverse of :meets. For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A starts exactly when B ends.

Relates each member of a jointly considered set of at least two time-series segments to the same Knowledge individual, where the proposition is meaningful or valid only with respect to that segment set collectively and cannot be represented as independent knowledge assertions for its individual members. Generation inputs are provenance and do not by themselves determine this collective scope.
Opposed to Input Knowledge, this property defines the knowledge included in the output of a Knowledge generation Entity.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'overlappedBy' (OWL-Time time:intervalOverlappedBy). Inverse of :overlaps. For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A is overlapped by B.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'overlaps' (OWL-Time time:intervalOverlaps). For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A starts before B and ends during B (partial overlap).
Defines the concept of a particular Knowledge Quality Measure.
Defines the dimensions associated with a Time Series Segment. Multiple dimensions indicate that the segment corresponds to a multivariate time series.
Defines the index associated with a Time Series Segment. Inherits from the time:TemporalEntity.
Relates any Knowledge available for a particular Time Series Segment.

Allen’s interval algebra relation 'startedBy' (OWL-Time time:intervalStartedBy). Inverse of :starts. For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A is started by B, both start together and B finishes before A.
Allen’s interval algebra relation 'starts' (OWL-Time time:intervalStarts). For TimeSeriesSegment individuals, inferable via :segmentIndex: A and B share the same start, and A finishes before B.
Can be used to optionally add a title to an entity of the domain.
Relates a KnowledgeGenerationEntity to an input it used. Specialisation of prov:used.
The string representation of a concrete EmbeddedValue. Its datatype is specified through hasDatatype.
Relates a KnowledgeGenerationOutput to the input it was derived from. Specialisation of prov:wasDerivedFrom.
